Whole-arc movers

Who the pedigree-conditional charge has hurt, who it has helped, and by how much — across the entire arc rather than the last step. ORDER K is the last board before this mechanism path began; ORDER P is where the charge was introduced; the ORDER R boards are the softening the owner ruled. Nothing here is adopted and nothing lands.

Read rank, not points

The board totals are different numbers. ORDER K totals 673,097 and ORDER P totals 666,434 — 6,663 fewer points spread across the same 804 players. Most rows therefore fall in absolute terms for a reason that has nothing to do with any individual player: there are simply fewer points on the board to go round.

Rank is the fair comparison across these boards. Absolute points are not. Both are shown; the rank-change columns are the ones to read when comparing one board with another.

The spanning variant is not a recommendation

The “softening” and “whole arc” columns use R20b2A — ORDER R p20 0.105 A ON — softest + FIX A. It is the far corner of the grid: both levers at their softest. It was chosen because it spans the arc, not because this seat prefers it. This seat recommends nothing.

Every other variant carries its own value, rank and charge columns in the ledger below and in ARC_R.csv.

Every row, sorted by the whole-arc move

Sorted by the size of R20b2A minus ORDER K, largest first, so the biggest movers in both directions sit at the top. Rank 1 is the most valuable of the 804 rows, and a positive rank change means the row moved up the board. The player column stays put as you scroll sideways.

Mechanism diagnostics: PG is the pedigree premium at the row’s entry price, in points a game. s(age) is production against the S1 age bar alone; s(ped) is production against that bar plus the premium, which is what the charge actually reads. By construction s(ped) = s(age) − PG. The chg columns are the share of the pedigree leg removed on each board.
